summary: This note is a short encyclopedic overview of Togo, a small West African country bordered by Ghana, Benin and Burkina Faso, with its capital Lomé on the Gulf of Guinea. It notes Togo's small size and population of about one million. It also describes Togo's linguistic diversity, with 39 languages spoken, French as the sole official language, and Ewé and Kabiyé designated national languages in 1975.
one_line: Overview of Togo, a small West African country on the Gulf of Guinea, and its multilingual population and language policy.
key_facts: Togo is officially the Togolese Republic.
Togo is a country in West Africa bordered by Ghana to the west, Benin to the east and Burkina Faso to the north.
Togo extends south to the Gulf of Guinea, where its capital Lomé is located.
Togo is one of the smallest countries in Africa.
Togo has a population of approximately 1 million.
According to Ethnologue, 39 distinct languages are spoken in Togo.
Many of Togo's languages are spoken by communities that number fewer than 100,000 members.
French is the sole official language of Togo.
In 1975, Ewé and Kabiyé were designated politically as national languages of Togo.
Ewé and Kabiyé are the two most widely spoken indigenous languages in Togo.
Ewé is also written as Èʋegbe in its native form and Evé in French.
